**Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) — Q1 2024 Business Analysis Briefing**
*For Fund Managers | Equity Research — May 2024*
*Quarter Ended March 31, 2024*

### Executive Summary: Quality Growth Over Scale

Tencent delivered a classic high-quality beat in Q1 2024: modest top-line growth paired with exceptional profit leverage.

> **Total Revenue: RMB 159.501bn, +6% YoY**
> **Gross Profit: RMB 83.870bn, +23% YoY; Gross Margin: 53% vs. 45% last year**
> **Non-IFRS Net Profit: RMB 50.265bn, +54% YoY**

The investment takeaway is clear: Tencent has shifted from a revenue-growth story to a margin-expansion and cash-compounding story. Profit grew 9x faster than revenue. The 8pp gross margin expansion is the single most important signal this quarter.

Three drivers explain it:
1. **Mix shift** toward high-margin Online Advertising (+26% YoY)
2. **Cost discipline and operating leverage** across cloud, games, and content
3. **Ecosystem monetization** — Video Accounts and Mini Programs are now material profit engines, not just user-time experiments.

Value-Added Services (VAS) remains the drag, but Advertising and FinTech & Business Services more than offset it.

### 1. Financial Snapshot

| Metric | Q1 2024 (RMB bn) | YoY | Comment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Revenue** | 159.501 | +6% | Steady, in-line with macro recovery |
| **VAS** | 78.629 | -0.9% | 49.3% of revenue; gaming transition |
| **Online Advertising** | 26.506 | +26% | 16.6% of revenue; fastest grower |
| **FinTech & Business Services** | 52.302 | +7% | 32.8% of revenue; resilient compounder |
| **Gross Profit** | 83.870 | +23% | Margin 53% |
| **Non-IFRS Net Profit** | 50.265 | +54% | Strong operating leverage |

Net profit margin (non-IFRS) is now ~31.5%, a level not seen since the pre-regulation peak. This is not one-off cost cutting — it reflects a structural change in revenue mix.

### 2. Deep Dive: Three Core Engines

#### A. Gaming: In Transition — Domestic Weakness Masked by International Resilience

Gaming remains inside VAS (RMB 78.629bn, -0.9% YoY), and explains the segment's decline.

* **Domestic Games: RMB 34.5bn, -2% YoY**
* **International Games: RMB 13.6bn, +3% YoY**

**Analysis for managers:**

1.  **Domestic is cyclical, not structural.** The -2% reflects a high base for evergreen titles like *Honor of Kings* and *Peacekeeper Elite* during a period with fewer major new launches in Q1. Regulatory overhang has largely normalized — the issue is product cycle, not licenses. User engagement remains stable, and deferred revenue remains healthy.

2.  **International provides diversification.** +3% growth, driven by Supercell portfolio recovery (notably *Brawl Stars* rebound) and sustained performance of *PUBG Mobile* and *VALORANT*. This validates Tencent's overseas studio strategy as a hedge against domestic cyclicality.

3.  **Profit > Revenue.** Despite the revenue dip, games gross margin improved due to a shift away from lower-margin licensed titles toward self-developed evergreens and tighter marketing spend.

**What to watch:** Pipeline is the catalyst. *Dungeon & Fighter Mobile* (launched May 2024) and renewed content for evergreen franchises are key to returning domestic games to low-single-digit to mid-single-digit growth in H2 2024. For valuation, do not penalize Tencent for a -2% quarter — focus on sustained 30%+ segment margins and strong free cash flow.

**Fund Manager View: NEUTRAL to POSITIVE.** Short-term soft, but troughing. International growth de-risks the segment.

#### B. Online Advertising: The Star Performer — Video Accounts Monetization Inflects

**Revenue: RMB 26.506bn, +26% YoY** — significantly outgrowing China's overall ad market (~10-12%).

This is Tencent's highest-margin business, and therefore the primary driver of the group-level margin expansion from 45% to 53%.

**Why it grew 26%:**

1.  **New inventory:** Video Accounts (Channels) user time spent **+80%+ YoY**. Tencent has successfully created a third major ad pillar alongside Moments and Official Accounts. Ad load is still relatively low vs. Douyin, leaving significant headroom for pricing and load increases through 2024-2025.

2.  **AI-enhanced targeting:** Upgrades to Tencent's advertising AI model improved click-through rates and ROI for advertisers, particularly in e-commerce, gaming, education, and local services. This drove both budget reallocation to Tencent and higher eCPMs.

3.  **Ecosystem closed-loop:** Mini Programs user time spent **+20%+ YoY**. Mini Programs + WeChat Pay + Video Accounts creates a full discovery-to-transaction loop. Advertisers are not just buying impressions; they are buying conversions inside WeChat, which commands a premium.

**Fund Manager View: STRONGLY POSITIVE.** Advertising is now a structural compounder. With Video Accounts still under-monetized relative to time spent, we see 2-3 years of above-market growth. Every incremental RMB of ad revenue drops disproportionately to gross profit. This is the core of the bullish margin thesis.

#### C. FinTech & Business Services: The Steady Compounder

**Revenue: RMB 52.302bn, +7% YoY**

Often overlooked, this is now one-third of Tencent and the backbone of WeChat's commercial ecosystem.

**Two sub-engines:**

1.  **FinTech (WeChat Pay, Wealth Management, Micro-loans):** Grew mid-single digits. Payment volume benefited from offline consumption recovery and Mini Programs transactions. Growth of +7% reflects a mature payments market and conservative consumer spending, not share loss. WeChat Pay maintains dominant offline share alongside Alipay. Wealth management (Licaitong) continues to grow AUM, providing stable fee income.

2.  **Business Services (Tencent Cloud, Enterprise SaaS):** Returned to healthy growth after the strategic shift from low-margin reselling to high-margin self-developed PaaS/SaaS. Highlight: **Tencent Cloud audio & video solutions maintained domestic market leadership for six consecutive years.** This signals pricing power in enterprise video, conferencing (Tencent Meeting), and CDN. AI-related cloud demand and large-model services are beginning to contribute.

Margin profile improved materially as loss-making cloud contracts were culled.

**Fund Manager View: POSITIVE.** 7% may look modest, but it is high-quality, recurring, and increasingly profitable. Think of it as Tencent's AWS + Visa hybrid: lower volatility, strong cash conversion, leveraged to China's digitalization and eventual consumption rebound.

### 3. Ecosystem Synergies: The Moat Widens

The non-financial KPIs confirm the WeChat flywheel is accelerating:

* **Tencent Video paid subs: 116 million, +8% YoY**
* **Tencent Music paid subs: 114 million, +20% YoY**

Both demonstrate pricing power in long-form content and music despite a tough consumer environment. Reduced content costs (fewer, higher-ROI dramas) + rising ARPPU = VAS margin uplift even as gaming revenue dipped.

Combined with Video Accounts +80% and Mini Programs +20% in time spent, Tencent has successfully extended user time from social/messaging to video, commerce, and services — all monetizable within its own payment loop without traffic acquisition costs.

### Investment Thesis & Outlook

**Thesis: Own Tencent for earnings leverage, not just revenue re-acceleration.**

1.  **Profitability inflection is structural.** A 53% gross margin is driven by mix (ads, high-margin games, SaaS) and efficiency, not one-offs. Non-IFRS net profit +54% shows operating leverage is intact.

2.  **Multiple growth options:** Ad load expansion, DNF Mobile and new game cycle, cloud AI monetization, and fintech recovery on consumption stimulus.

3.  **Capital return:** Strong cash flow supports continued buybacks and dividends, enhancing EPS growth beyond net profit growth.

**Key Risks to Monitor:**
* Macro consumption weakness capping payments and ad budgets from SMEs
* Game pipeline execution delays and regulatory shifts
* Competition in short video (Douyin) and cloud (Alibaba, Huawei)
* AI capex intensity pressuring near-term free cash flow

**Bottom Line for Portfolio Positioning:** Q1 2024 confirms Tencent as a core large-cap quality compounder. VAS softness is temporary and well-flagged; Advertising (+26%) and margin expansion (+8pp) are structural. Maintain OVERWEIGHT on earnings revision momentum into H2 2024, with catalysts from gaming launches and continued Video Accounts monetization.

---
*Disclaimer: This briefing is based on Tencent Holdings Limited Q1 2024 unaudited results for informational purposes for professional investors only and does not constitute investment advice or a recommendation.*

**Competitive Analysis Report on China's Leading Online Education Platforms: Yuanfudao vs. Zuoyebang**

**Reporting Period: 2022 - 2024 | Market Focus: China K-12 Online Education & Intelligent Learning Hardware**

### 1. Executive Summary

Following the 2021 "Double Reduction" policy, China's online education industry underwent a fundamental restructuring. Subject-based tutoring was curtailed, forcing former unicorns to pivot toward new growth curves: intelligent educational hardware, quality-oriented education (suzhi jiaoyu), and AI large-model technology.

This report analyzes the two undisputed leaders that successfully navigated the transition — **Yuanfudao (Ape Tutoring)** and **Zuoyebang (Homework Help)** — from the dimensions of market performance, product strategy, technology capability, and brand influence.

**Key Findings:**

1.  **Divergent Strategic Paths:** Zuoyebang has adopted a **Hardware-Led Commercialization** strategy, achieving dominant market share in learning tablets. Yuanfudao has adopted a **Technology & Data-Led** strategy, building deep moats in AI large models and educational content ecosystems.
2.  **Market Momentum vs. Technological Depth:** Zuoyebang leads in current sales conversion and omnichannel volume, while Yuanfudao leads in underlying R&D assets, enterprise recognition, and long-term AI application scenarios.
3.  **Future Competition:** The battleground has shifted from user acquisition for live classes to a three-dimensional war over: 1) Intelligent Hardware, 2) AI Tutoring Models, and 3) Ecosystem Loyalty.

### 2. Industry Background

China's learning tablet market has become the primary successor to online tutoring. With parents willing to pay for compliant, tech-enabled, at-home learning solutions, the market saw explosive growth in 2023-2024. Competition is no longer about teachers, but about algorithms, content libraries, and hardware-software integration.

Both Yuanfudao and Zuoyebang leveraged their massive historical user bases (hundreds of millions), question banks, and brand trust to enter this new arena.

### 3. Company Profiles & Strategic Positioning

#### 3.1 Zuoyebang: The Hardware Market Leader

Originally known for its photo-search problem-solving app, Zuoyebang has successfully transformed into China's No.1 intelligent education hardware brand.

Its strategy is characterized by rapid product iteration and aggressive omnichannel sales. Zuoyebang launched multiple products in the educational hardware sector, such as learning machines and learning watches, maintaining frequent iterations to meet market demands. This product matrix covers preschool enlightenment to K12 synchronous learning, creating a closed-loop hardware family.

#### 3.2 Yuanfudao: The Technology-Driven Ecosystem Player

Yuanfudao Group, parent of brands including Yuantiku, Xiaoyuan Kousuan, Zebra AI, and Guava, has positioned itself as a technology-driven education science company.

Rather than focusing solely on single-device sales, Yuanfudao emphasizes underlying capabilities and diversified business lines including smart hardware (Xiaoyuan Learning Machine), digital publishing, and offline literacy centers. Its influence extends beyond education into the broader internet and cultural economy.

This is evidenced by its corporate honors: In 2022, Yuanfudao was recognized as one of China's top 100 comprehensive internet companies, demonstrating its competitive strength and innovative leadership in the internet industry. In 2024, Yuanfudao was further selected for the "Beijing Top 100 Private Enterprises" and "Top 100 Cultural Industries" lists, demonstrating its significant position and influence in the capital's economy.

### 4. Head-to-Head Comparison: Market Performance

This is where Zuoyebang currently demonstrates a clear, quantifiable lead.

**Zuoyebang's Market Dominance (2024 Data):**

According to market data from various platforms:

> Zuoyebang achieved a 20.6% online market share in Q3 2024, with sales volume growing over 300% year-on-year, demonstrating strong market momentum.

This triple-digit growth in a highly competitive market indicates exceptional product-market fit, effective Douyin/Tmall/JD live-commerce strategy, and strong word-of-mouth among parents.

More importantly, its leadership is not limited to online:

> From January to November 2024, Zuoyebang ranked first in national sales volume in China's learning tablet market across all channels (online + offline).

Ranking No.1 across all channels for an 11-month period proves that Zuoyebang has successfully cracked both e-commerce traffic and offline dealer networks (Suning, department stores, franchise experience stores) — a feat its competitors have struggled to replicate.

Yuanfudao, while also a top-3 player in learning machines with its Xiaoyuan brand, has not publicly disclosed comparable share leadership in 2024, suggesting it trails Zuoyebang in pure hardware volume, but compensates with higher user activity in its software apps (Xiaoyuan Kousuan remains a national-level tool app).

### 5. Head-to-Head Comparison: Technology & R&D

This is where Yuanfudao holds a distinct advantage.

**Yuanfudao's AI and Data Moat:**

Yuanfudao is driven by both technology and data. The Group possesses high-quality educational datasets covering 1 billion questions, with large model training parameters reaching 70 billion levels, integrating multiple types of data including text, images, language, and video, creating extensive educational application scenarios for large model technology.

Analysis:
*   **1 Billion Questions:** This is an almost unreplicable asset accumulated over a decade of online tutoring. It provides clean, labeled, step-by-step problem-solving logic for AI training.
*   **70 Billion Parameters:** This places Yuanfudao's educational large model at the forefront of vertical-domain models in China, far exceeding general-purpose models in accuracy for math reasoning, essay correction, and oral dialogue.
*   **Multimodal Integration:** By integrating text, images, language, and video, Yuanfudao can power features like photo-based error analysis, AI oral English companions, and video explanation generation — directly embedded into its learning machines and apps.

Zuoyebang also invests heavily in AI (its Silverleaf large model), but its public narrative is more product-application oriented (e.g., AI Q&A, AI composition tutoring) rather than foundational model parameters and dataset scale. Zuoyebang wins on *application speed*; Yuanfudao wins on *technological depth*.

### 6. SWOT Analysis

**Zuoyebang**
*   **Strengths:** No.1 omnichannel sales volume; 20.6% online share; 300%+ YoY growth; rapid hardware iteration (learning machines + watches); strong parent trust.
*   **Weaknesses:** Over-reliance on hardware sales cycles; high marketing/channel costs to maintain growth; perceived as less deep in foundational AI research vs. Yuanfudao.
*   **Opportunities:** Expand into AI wearables for children, overseas Chinese learning market, subscription-based content services attached to hardware.
*   **Threats:** Price wars with iFLYTEK, Xiaodu, and Yuanfudao; hardware homogenization.

**Yuanfudao**
*   **Strengths:** Massive 1B-question data asset; 70B-parameter large model; strong government/industry recognition (Beijing Top 100 Private/Cultural, Top 100 Internet); diversified matrix (Zebra, Xiaoyuan, Guava).
*   **Weaknesses:** Hardware sales volume lags behind Zuoyebang; complex business lines dilute focus; monetization of large-model technology is still long-term.
*   **Opportunities:** B2B licensing of educational AI models to schools/publishers; AI-driven personalized learning as SaaS; cultural IP expansion.
*   **Threats:** Slower commercialization may cede hardware mindshare; regulatory scrutiny on AI content for minors.

### 7. Competitive Matrix Summary

| Dimension | Zuoyebang | Yuanfudao | Leader |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Q3 2024 Online Share** | 20.6%, +300% YoY | Top-tier, but lower | **Zuoyebang** |
| **Jan-Nov 2024 All-Channel Volume** | National No.1 | Top 3 | **Zuoyebang** |
| **Product Strategy** | Frequent iteration: Learning Machine, Learning Watch | Ecosystem: Hardware + Apps + Literacy Centers | **Zuoyebang (Speed)** |
| **Core Tech Asset** | Applied AI for tutoring | 1B questions, 70B-parameter multimodal model | **Yuanfudao** |
| **Brand Recognition** | Market sales leader | Beijing Top 100 Private, Top 100 Cultural, Top 100 Internet | **Yuanfudao** |

### 8. Outlook and Strategic Recommendations

The competition between the two giants will define the next five years of Chinese EdTech:

1.  **For Zuoyebang:** Must convert its hardware sales lead into long-term software retention. With over 300% growth, the priority is to reduce churn by building a paid content membership system, preventing devices from becoming "one-time purchases."
2.  **For Yuanfudao:** Must translate its technological and reputational advantages into market share. Its 70B-parameter model and multimodal capabilities need a killer hardware form factor to challenge Zuoyebang's No.1 position. Leveraging its "Cultural Industries Top 100" status to create proprietary quality-education IP could be a differentiator.
3.  **Industry Trend:** The ultimate winner will be whoever best integrates Yuanfudao-style deep AI (understanding a student's learning) with Zuoyebang-style superior hardware and channels (delivering that learning to the desk).

**Conclusion:** Currently, **Zuoyebang is the commercial champion** of the post-Double Reduction era, while **Yuanfudao is the technology and ecosystem champion**. Investors seeking short-term ROI will favor Zuoyebang's momentum; those betting on long-term AI in education will favor Yuanfudao's data moat.

**Pet Love Life: Protecting Every Companionship, Caring for Every Life**

In a warm, sunlit home, a lively puppy plays by the window. He jumps, spins, and wags his tail, his bright eyes following every movement of his owner. She looks back at him tenderly, her heart full of love and gratitude — because he is not just a pet, but family. A companion who shares her mornings, her laughter, and her quiet evenings.

It is this deep, everyday connection that inspired Pet Love Life. We exist for one simple reason: so every pet can grow up healthy and happy, and every pet parent can feed them with complete peace of mind.

### It All Began With Our Own Pets

Pet Love Life didn't start in a boardroom. It started in our living rooms.

Our founder, a lifelong dog lover, adopted a Golden Retriever named Sunny. Like many owners, she trusted the beautiful packaging on store shelves — until Sunny began suffering from chronic allergies, dull fur, and digestive problems. After months of vet visits, the cause became clear: inferior ingredients, vague meat by-products, and artificial additives hidden in his everyday food.

At the same time, our co-founder, a veterinary nutritionist and cat dad to two rescue cats, Mimi and Tofu, was seeing the same story in his clinic every day: pets with obesity, kidney strain, and skin issues linked directly to poor nutrition.

We asked ourselves a painful question: *If we can't trust what's in their bowl, how can we protect them?*

So we made a promise to Sunny, Mimi, and Tofu — to create the food we wished existed. We gathered veterinarians, pet nutrition scientists, and fellow pet parents, and spent nearly three years in kitchens, farms, and labs. We tasted, tested, rejected hundreds of formulas, and watched our own pets become our first and most honest critics. When Sunny's coat turned glossy again and his energy returned, we knew we were on the right path. That journey became Pet Love Life.

### Natural Ingredients, Crafted With Science and Love

From day one, we decided: only what we would proudly feed our own pets would ever carry our name.

Every Pet Love Life recipe starts with real, traceable, human-grade ingredients. We partner directly with certified family farms and sustainable fisheries we know by name — for free-range chicken, wild-caught salmon, grass-fed beef, plus farm-fresh vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. No meat meals of unknown origin. No fillers. No compromises.

In collaboration with leading pet nutrition research institutes, every formula is designed to meet and exceed AAFCO nutritional standards for different life stages, breeds, and needs — from playful puppies and kittens to gentle seniors. We balance high-quality animal protein, healthy fats rich in Omega-3 & 6, natural fiber, vitamins, and minerals to support immunity, digestion, skin and coat, joints, and heart health.

Our goal was never just to provide "enough to eat." It is to provide food that helps them *thrive* — delicious in taste, complete in nutrition.

### Safety You Can See: Our Strict Control Standards

Love alone is not enough. Trust must be earned with transparency and rigor. That's why we built a farm-to-bowl safety system with specific, verifiable measures:

**1. 5-Step Ingredient Screening:** Every batch of raw material undergoes origin verification, pesticide and heavy-metal testing, microbiological screening, nutritional analysis, and freshness grading. If it fails even one test, it never enters our factory.

**2. 128 Quality Checkpoints:** From grinding and low-temperature slow cooking that locks in nutrients, to sealing and packaging, each bag passes 128 checkpoints. Our entire process is 100% pollution-free, with zero artificial colors, flavors, preservatives, or GMOs.

**3. Third-Party Testing & Full Traceability:** Every finished batch is sent to independent SGS-certified laboratories for safety testing before shipping. And we publish those reports. Simply scan the QR code on any bag to see exactly where your pet's food came from, its nutritional report, and its production date.

**4. Feeding Trials With Vets, Not Just Labs:** Before any new product launches, we conduct palatability tests and long-term feeding trials under the supervision of veterinarians and nutritionists to ensure it is safe, digestible, and truly loved by pets.

We also open our factory doors with live tours and open-day events, because we have nothing to hide. What you see is what your pet eats.

### Beyond the Bowl: Caring for Stray Lives

We firmly believe pets are not just companions — they are life, deserving of respect. And while our pets sleep warmly at home, millions of stray animals are still waiting for kindness.

That's why caring for strays is written into our mission, not just our marketing:

**One Bag, One Meal Project:** For every bag of Pet Love Life you purchase, we donate a nutritious meal to a shelter pet. To date, we have donated over 2 million meals in partnership with 120+ rescue shelters across the country.

**Pet Love Life Angel Fund:** We dedicate 1% of our annual revenue to fund free spay/neuter programs, emergency medical rescue, vaccinations, and winter shelter supplies for stray cats and dogs.

**Home for Homeless Tails Adoption Days:** Every month, we host adoption events with veterinarians on-site, providing free first-year health checkups, starter food kits, and training guidance for new families. Over 3,800 strays have found forever homes through this program.

**Pet Health Classrooms:** Our vet team regularly visits communities, schools, and shelters to share scientific feeding knowledge and responsible pet ownership, helping more people raise pets with love and understanding.

**Customer Churn Analysis Report**
**Q4 2024 (October 1 - December 31, 2024)**

**Prepared by: Customer Operations & Sales Management**
**Date: January 8, 2025**
**To: Company Management**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

In Q4 2024, the Company lost a total of **8 customers**, with a total direct loss of **1,320,000 Yuan**.

Churn accelerated significantly during the quarter, from 2 customers in October, to 2 in November, to 4 in December. December alone accounted for 50% of churned accounts.

Analysis shows churn was highly concentrated and preventable. The three main controllable drivers — **Price Factors, Service Issues, and Product Mismatch** — each accounted for 25% of churned customers, together representing 75% of all losses. Product Mismatch caused the highest single-category loss at 370,000 Yuan, while the single largest loss was Kaiyue Group (C008, 300,000 Yuan) due to restructuring.

This report provides a detailed breakdown by reason, department, time, and loss value, identifies root causes, and proposes targeted retention and improvement actions for Q1 2025.

### 2. Churn Overview - Key Metrics

| KPI | Q4 2024 Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Number of Churned Customers** | 8 |
| **Total Loss Amount** | 1,320,000 Yuan |
| **Average Loss per Customer** | 165,000 Yuan |
| **Peak Churn Month** | December (4 customers) |
| **Departments Most Affected** | Sales Dept. (3 customers), Customer Service (2 customers) |

### 3. Detailed Churn Records

| ID | Customer Name | Churn Date | Churn Reason | Loss (Yuan) | Related Dept. | Remarks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| C001 | Oriental Manufacturing Co., Ltd. | 2024-10-05 | Product price too high | 150,000 | Sales Dept. | Price adjustment request couldn't reach agreement |
| C002 | Shengda Electric Company | 2024-10-18 | Long service response time | 90,000 | Customer Service | Switched to competitor, demanding faster support response |
| C003 | Future Smart Technology Co. | 2024-11-01 | Customization needs not met | 250,000 | Project Dept. | Needs more flexible product customization solutions |
| C004 | Blue Ocean Electronics Co., Ltd. | 2024-11-15 | Lack of innovative products | 120,000 | Product Dept. | Product features lag behind market demands |
| C005 | Starlight Precision Manufacturing | 2024-12-02 | Intense market competition | 180,000 | Sales Dept. | Lost due to competitor's pricing advantage |
| C006 | Huateng Automation Co., Ltd. | 2024-12-10 | Unclear contract terms | 200,000 | Legal Dept. | Disputed contract terms, failed to renew |
| C007 | Anda Technology Company | 2024-12-20 | Unsatisfactory after-sales service | 80,000 | Customer Service | Complained about poor after-sales quality, changed supplier |
| C008 | Kaiyue Group | 2024-12-25 | Company restructuring, suspended purchases | 300,000 | Sales Dept. | Suspended all purchases due to restructuring |

### 4. Analysis by Churn Reason

Churn reasons fall into five categories:

**1. Price Factors: 2 customers (25%), 330,000 Yuan**
Represented by C001 Oriental Manufacturing (150,000) and C005 Starlight Precision (180,000). Customers are highly sensitive to price rigidity and competitor undercutting. The Sales Dept. lacked flexible pricing authority and a rapid approval mechanism, leading to failed negotiations.

**2. Service Issues: 2 customers (25%), 270,000 Yuan**
Represented by C002 Shengda Electric (long response time) and C007 Anda Technology (poor after-sales quality). Both customers explicitly switched suppliers for better service. This points to systemic problems: no SLA for response time, insufficient after-sales follow-up, and poor service quality control.

**3. Product Mismatch: 2 customers (25%), 370,000 Yuan - Highest Loss Category**
Represented by C003 Future Smart Technology (250,000, customization not met) and C004 Blue Ocean Electronics (120,000, lack of innovation). Although equal in number, this category caused the largest financial impact. It reflects a gap between our standardized products and market demand for flexible customization and continuous innovation.

**4. Competition Factors: 1 customer (12.5%), 180,000 Yuan**
Starlight Precision Manufacturing was lost directly to a competitor's pricing advantage. This highlights weak competitive intelligence and value-based selling — we competed on price alone rather than on total value, service, and technology.

**5. Contract Issues: 1 customer (12.5%), 200,000 Yuan**
Huateng Automation (200,000) failed to renew due to unclear contract terms. Legal and sales alignment was insufficient during signing and renewal, creating distrust at a critical moment.

> **Special Note:** C008 Kaiyue Group (300,000 Yuan, the largest single loss) churned due to external restructuring and suspension of purchases. This is non-controllable in the short term, but represents a high-potential win-back opportunity once restructuring is complete.

### 5. Analysis by Department and Time

**By Responsible Department:**
*   **Sales Dept.: 3 customers (C001, C005, C008)** - Highest exposure. Needs stronger pricing tools, competitor response playbooks, and key-account maintenance for restructuring clients.
*   **Customer Service: 2 customers (C002, C007)** - Both service-related. Urgent need for response-time standards and after-sales quality audits.
*   **Project Dept.: 1 customer (C003, 250,000)** - High-value customization failure.
*   **Product Dept.: 1 customer (C004)** - Innovation lag.
*   **Legal Dept.: 1 customer (C006, 200,000)** - Contract clarity and renewal process failure.

**By Time Trend - A Warning Signal:**
*   **October: 2 customers** - Early price and service warnings.
*   **November: 2 customers** - Shift to product capability issues, with higher average loss.
*   **December: 4 customers** - Churn doubled. Year-end renewal period, budget freezes, and competitor year-end promotions intensified losses.

The trend shows churn is not isolated but accelerating.

**By Loss Concentration:**
The top 3 losses — Kaiyue Group (300,000), Future Smart (250,000), and Huateng Automation (200,000) — account for 750,000 Yuan, or **56.8% of total quarterly loss**. Retention of high-value accounts must be prioritized.

### 6. Key Findings and Root Causes

1.  **No Early-Warning System:** 6 of 8 customers showed prior signals (price complaints, service tickets, customization requests) but were not flagged as at-risk.
2.  **Price Rigidity vs. Value Communication:** Sales lacks tiered pricing and authorization to match competitors while defending value.
3.  **Service SLA Missing:** "Long response time" and "poor after-sales" are repeatable, measurable failures.
4.  **Product-Market Gap:** Standard products cannot meet demands for flexible customization and rapid iteration.
5.  **Contract Risk at Renewal:** Legal terms become a churn trigger 60-90 days before renewal if not reviewed proactively.

### 7. Recommendations and Action Plan for Q1 2025

**Immediate Actions (30 days):**
1.  **Win-Back Task Force (Owner: Sales Dept.):** Maintain monthly contact with Kaiyue Group to track restructuring progress; prepare a restart offer. Re-approach Oriental Manufacturing with a revised tiered quotation.
2.  **Service SLA (Owner: Customer Service):** Implement 4-hour first response / 24-hour solution commitment; publish weekly response-time dashboard; conduct service回访 for all Top 20 accounts.
3.  **Contract Audit (Owner: Legal + Sales):** Review all contracts expiring in next 6 months; standardize key terms in plain language; initiate renewal talks 90 days in advance. Priority: prevent a repeat of C006.

**Short-Term Improvements (1-3 months):**
4.  **Flexible Pricing Mechanism (Owner: Sales + Finance):** Establish three-level discount approval authority and a competitor-price reporting system. Shift from price competition to total-cost-of-ownership selling.
5.  **Product Rapid Response (Owner: Product + Project Dept.):** Launch a modular customization solution package for needs like C003; publish Q1 product innovation roadmap to address feedback like C004; hold monthly Voice-of-Customer meetings.
6.  **At-Risk Customer List (Owner: All Depts.):** Score all active customers on price sensitivity, service tickets, contract expiry, and competitor contact. Assign owners for red-flag accounts.

**Target for Q1 2025:** Reduce churned customers by 50%, reduce churn loss to under 600,000 Yuan, and achieve zero churn due to service response time.

### 8. Conclusion

Q4 churn of 8 customers and 1,320,000 Yuan is a significant loss, but 87.5% of cases (excluding restructuring) were controllable internal issues of price, service, product, and contract.

December's spike must be treated as a management alert. If pricing flexibility, service standards, product customization, and contract management are systematically improved, and if the relationship with Kaiyue Group is preserved for future recovery, the Company can reverse the trend in Q1 2025 and turn churn analysis into retention growth.

We recommend management approve the above action plan and review progress monthly.

### ChatGPT Concept Stocks: A Detailed Investment Opportunity Analysis for Individual Investors

> **Disclaimer:** This analysis is for educational and informational purposes only. It is not investment advice, not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI-related stocks are highly volatile. Please do your own due diligence and consult a licensed financial advisor before making investment decisions.

As an individual investor, you are looking at the right place at the right time — but also at the most crowded place. Since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022, "ChatGPT concept" has evolved from a short-term hype theme into a full-blown AI industrial revolution spanning chips, cloud, data, models, and applications.

The key question in 2026 is no longer *“Will AI work?”* but *“Who will actually make money from AI, and at what price are you paying for that future profit?”*

Here is a complete breakdown to help you think like a professional.

#### 1. What Are "ChatGPT Concept Stocks"?

"ChatGPT concept stocks" does not refer to one company. It refers to all listed companies that are expected to benefit from the commercialization of generative AI and large language models (LLMs).

The market generally divides them into 4 layers:

**The AI Value Chain Map:**

1.  **Infrastructure Layer (Selling Shovels):** Computing power, chips, servers, networking, data centers, power supply
2.  **Model & Platform Layer (Building Engines):** Foundation model developers, cloud platforms, AI development tools
3.  **Data Layer (Supplying Fuel):** Data providers, data annotation, copyrighted corpus, data security
4.  **Application Layer (Selling Cars):** AI search, office software, gaming, advertising, education, healthcare, e-commerce, enterprise services, AI hardware (AI PC, AI phone)

In the early stage (2023-2024), money was made in Layer 1. In 2025-2026, the focus is shifting to Layer 2 and Layer 4 — who can turn traffic into revenue.

#### 2. Where Are the Real Opportunities? Track by Track

**Track A: Computing Power - The Most Certain, But Most Crowded**

This is the core beneficiary of ChatGPT. Training and inference of models like GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude, and Llama require massive GPU clusters.

*   **Logic:** AI demand = chip demand = server demand = optical module + IDC + liquid cooling + power demand. Performance is visible in financial reports.
*   **Representative types:** GPU designers (e.g., NVIDIA, AMD), AI server OEMs, cloud infrastructure providers (Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud), optical transceiver makers, IDC operators, chip foundries.
*   **Pros:** Real orders, real revenue, high barriers to entry.
*   **Cons for 2026:** Valuations are already very high. The market is now debating: shift from Training to Inference, domestic substitution, and whether hyperscaler CAPEX can continue to grow 30%+ YoY. High cyclicality.

**Individual Investor Takeaway:** This is the "core asset" of AI investing. Suitable as a long-term core holding, but do not chase highs after earnings surges. Pay close attention to inventory, gross margin, and CAPEX guidance from Big Tech.

**Track B: Foundation Models & Cloud Giants - The Platform Winners**

OpenAI itself is not listed, but its ecosystem partners are.

*   **Logic:** "Winner-takes-most" in platforms. Companies with massive user base + cloud + capital can monetize AI via subscription (Copilot, Gemini Advanced) and API calls.
*   **Representative types:** Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Apple, plus leading local players like Baidu, Alibaba, Tencent, and vertical model leaders like Palantir.
*   **Pros:** Strong cash flow to sustain R&D, diversified business to cushion AI failure, clear monetization path.
*   **Cons:** Huge market caps mean slower growth. AI revenue is still <10-15% of total revenue for most giants. Regulatory and antitrust risks are rising.

**Individual Investor Takeaway:** This is the safest way for beginners to participate. If you can only pick one track, start here.

**Track C: Data Assets - The Underestimated Fuel**

ChatGPT cannot exist without high-quality data. As models move to multimodal (text + image + video + code) and AI Agents, demand for copyrighted, vertical, and private domain data is exploding.

*   **Logic:** Companies with exclusive data (financial data, legal, medical, academic publishing, mapping) + data annotation services will charge "data tolls."
*   **Pros:** Light assets, high margins, policy support for data elements as assets.
*   **Cons:** Copyright lawsuits, data privacy regulation (EU AI Act, US executive orders), and data quality is hard for retail investors to verify.

**Track D: AI Applications - Highest Elasticity, Highest Risk**

This is where 10-baggers *and* the most traps are. It includes: AI Office, AI Search, AI Marketing, AI Gaming, AI Education, AI Healthcare, AI Customer Service, AI Coding.

*   **Logic:** Low marginal cost. Once Product-Market-Fit is found, profits explode. Example: AI coding tools, AI marketing content generation, AI companions.
*   **Pros:** Huge market space, explosive stock price if successful.
*   **Cons:** 90% of "ChatGPT concept stocks" that just issued a press release belong here. No technology moat, high customer churn, competition from giants who can offer it for free. Many A-share / small-cap concept stocks have surged 200% then fallen 70% with no profit.

**Individual Investor Takeaway:** This is a *satellite* position, not a core position. Only invest in companies where you can see: 1) Daily Active Users growth, 2) Paying conversion rate, 3) ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) from AI, not just "we are developing a large model."

**Track E: AI Edge Hardware**

New in 2024-2026: AI PC, AI Phone, AI Glasses, smart speakers, humanoid robots. The logic is that LLMs will drive a new hardware replacement cycle.

This track is more cyclical and supply-chain driven. Watch for actual shipment volumes, not concept launches.

#### 3. How to Pick Stocks and Avoid "Concept Traps"

As a retail investor, you don't have an advantage in information speed, but you have an advantage in patience and selectivity. Use this 5-point checklist:

**1. Is it Real or Rubbing the Concept?**
Ask: What % of revenue came from AI last quarter? If a company has talked about "ChatGPT" for 2 years but AI revenue is still <5% and R&D staff hasn't grown, avoid it.

**2. Who Pays?**
Good business model = someone is willing to pay. Distinguish:
B2B (selling to enterprises via API/cloud) > B2C subscription > B2G projects > Pure traffic story with no monetization.

**3. What is the Moat?**
Chips: patents + ecosystem (CUDA)
Cloud giants: capital + users + data
Applications: exclusive scenario data + workflow integration + switching costs. A simple chatbot wrapper has NO moat.

**4. Financial Health**
AI burns cash. Check: Free cash flow, gross margin trend, R&D intensity, customer concentration. Avoid companies that hype AI while their main business is losing money and they keep issuing new shares.

**5. Valuation Method**
Traditional P/E often fails for high-growth AI stocks. Professionals use:
For giants: PEG + DCF with cloud growth
For infrastructure: P/E + Order backlog / PS
For SaaS applications: P/S + EV/Sales vs. ARR growth rate (Rule of 40)
If a loss-making small-cap is trading at 20x sales with no growth, you are paying for a perfect future that may never come.

#### 4. Risks You Must Understand

1.  **Hype Cycle Risk:** ChatGPT concept stocks are classic thematic speculation. After every surge comes a 30-50% pullback to kill leveraged retail traders.
2.  **Technology Iteration Risk:** Today's leader can be disrupted tomorrow. Model costs are falling 80%+ per year. Companies relying on a single model advantage are fragile.
3.  **Regulation & Geopolitics:** AI safety regulation, data copyright lawsuits, and US-China chip export controls directly impact supply chains and valuations.
4.  **Commercialization Gap:** Traffic ≠ Profit. Many AI products have high user numbers but huge inference costs, leading to "the more users, the more losses."
5.  **Liquidity Risk for Small Caps:** Many pure concept stocks have small floats and are easily manipulated.

#### 5. A Rational Strategy for Individual Investors

Don't try to bet on one winner. Think in portfolios:

**A Core-Satellite Approach (Illustrative Example, Not Advice):**

*   **60% Core - Broad Exposure:** AI-themed ETFs, Nasdaq / S&P 500 index funds, or 2-3 cloud + chip leaders. Goal: capture beta, reduce single-stock risk.
*   **30% Growth - Value Chain Leaders:** Pick 3-5 companies in computing power, optical modules, or enterprise SaaS where you understand the financials. Buy in tranches.
*   **10% (Max) Satellite - High-Risk Application Bets:** Small positions in AI applications you actually use and like. Set a strict stop-loss (e.g., -15% to -20%) and take-profit discipline.

**Three Practical Rules:**

1.  **Invest in Batches, Not All-In:** Use dollar-cost averaging on pullbacks. Never chase a 20% limit-up day driven by news.
2.  **Set Your Time Horizon:** Infrastructure = 2-3 year logic. Applications = quarterly earnings verification. If you are short-term, reduce position size.
3.  **Track 3 Leading Indicators Monthly:** a) Hyperscaler CAPEX (Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon earnings calls), b) NVIDIA supply chain and lead times, c) Top AI App rankings and pricing changes.

> The best question to ask before buying is not "How high can it go?" but "If it drops 40% tomorrow, do I dare to buy more because I understand its profit source?"

#### 6. Outlook: What’s Next After ChatGPT?

In 2026, the market has moved beyond simple chatbots. Three directions deserve long-term attention:

1.  **AI Agents + Workflow Automation:** From "answering questions" to "doing tasks" in office, coding, customer service, and marketing. This is where enterprise budgets are flowing.
2.  **Inference & Cost Reduction:** As training costs stabilize, companies that provide cheaper inference (ASIC chips, optimization software, edge computing) will gain share.
3.  **Multimodal & Video (Sora-type) + Embodied AI:** Video generation, AI glasses, and robotics open new data and hardware markets, but commercialization is still early.

**Bottom Line:** ChatGPT concept stocks are not a sprint, but a 5-10 year industrial trend similar to the mobile internet in 2010. Short-term speculators pay for volatility; long-term investors get paid for identifying companies with real orders, real users, and real cash flow.

Start with giants and ETFs to learn, use small money to study applications, keep learning about the technology, and never invest money you cannot afford to lose.

If you’d like, tell me your risk tolerance (conservative / balanced / aggressive), investment amount range, and whether you prefer US stocks, A-shares, or ETFs, and I can help you build a personalized research checklist and observation list.

Secret 1: The Art of Time Management

Like martial arts masters who distribute their internal energy with precision, smart time allocation is the first step to balancing work and life. Learn to distinguish between urgent and important tasks, make a daily priority list, and focus on high-value work during your peak energy hours. Effective rest is like healing qigong, restoring body and mind with gentle power. Ensure sufficient sleep, persist in exercise, and cultivate a hobby that makes you happy — reading, music, hiking, or tea with friends. Establish a regular self-reflection mechanism, such as a weekly review or a quiet evening walk, to detect imbalance at its early stage. Like martial artists meditating daily, professionals need to continuously adjust their mindset, practice gratitude, and cherish the present moment. For our Group, which is primarily built around the GAC Toyota and FAW Toyota networks, October was a month of “volume stabilized by price, profit sacrificed for traffic.” At Group level, we retailed 1,286 new cars, down 7.4% MoM and down 12.8% YoY. The Highlander now offers up to RMB 80,000 off, bringing a RMB 325,800 flagship model down to RMB 245,800, a price level unimaginable three years ago when customers had to pay a premium of RMB 20,000-30,000 and wait three months. | Tesla | 62,100 | 4.08% | 3.95% | +0.13 pp |

Three key trends emerge:

**First, Toyota and Honda are losing share in lockstep, but Toyota shows stronger resilience.** Toyota’s October share of 6.96% is down 2.89pp YoY, almost identical to Honda’s 2.85pp drop. However, on a MoM basis, Toyota’s decline (-0.52pp) was larger than Honda’s (-0.31pp) because we increased discounts aggressively in September for the National Day auto show, pulling forward some demand. Cumulatively, Toyota still leads Honda by 2.27pp (7.42% vs. 5.15%), and the gap has actually widened slightly versus last year. This shows that among Japanese joint ventures, Toyota’s hybrid strategy (HEV) is still more accepted in Zhejiang than Honda’s, especially for Camry, Highlander and Sienna. Honda’s core fuel models – CR-V, Accord, Civic – have been hit harder by BYD Song PLUS DM-i, Seal 06, and Tesla Model Y.

**Second, Volkswagen is stabilizing at around 8.5-9.0%, defending better than Japanese brands.** Volkswagen’s YoY share loss (-2.85pp in Oct, -2.71pp cumulative) is similar to Toyota’s, but its MoM trend is flatter. The reason is Volkswagen’s faster NEV transformation in the region: the ID.3 and ID.4 CROZZ are now offering terminal discounts of RMB 60,000-70,000, with the ID.3 dropping to around RMB 120,000 on the road in Hangzhou, which has captured young first-time buyers who might otherwise have considered the Frontlander or Corolla Cross. Meanwhile, fuel models like Lavida, Passat and Tiguan L maintain fleet and middle-aged private buyer loyalty through 50,000-60,000 discounts. Volkswagen’s dual-track approach is worth learning from.

**Third, the market is now a “BYD + Geely + Tesla” squeeze on the RMB 100,000-250,000 core.** BYD alone took 18.4% in October, equivalent to Toyota + Honda + Tesla combined. In our price monitoring, the BYD Song PLUS DM-i Honor Edition (RMB 129,800-169,800 guide) directly suppresses Wildlander and RAV4; the BYD Han DM-i (RMB 169,800-225,800) and Seal 06 DM-i (RMB 99,800-139,800) sandwich the Camry from above and below; the BYD Tang DM-i (RMB 179,800-269,800) directly impacts Highlander and Venza. Geely’s Galaxy and Lynk & Co brands are also eroding our SUV base in third- and fourth-tier cities in Zhejiang (Wenzhou, Jinhua).

In summary, the annual trend is not a cyclical fluctuation but a structural shift. Joint-venture fuel and HEV market share in Zhejiang has fallen from 32.5% (Jan-Oct 2023) to 24.1% (Jan-Oct 2024). If we cannot accelerate the introduction of intelligent hybrid + intelligent cockpit selling points, and rely solely on price cuts, market share will continue to bleed 0.2-0.3pp per month.

### II. Group Store Performance Analysis: New Cars, Used Cars, After-Sales

Our Group operates four Toyota stores in Zhejiang: Hangzhou Chengxi Flagship Store (GAC Toyota), Ningbo Yinzhou Store (FAW Toyota), Wenzhou Ouhai Store (GAC Toyota), and Shaoxing Keqiao Store (FAW Toyota). Total staff 412.

#### 2.1 New Car Sales: Volume Down, Structure Differentiated

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hangzhou Chengxi | 428 | 462 | 485 | -7.4% | -11.8% | 89.2% |
| Ningbo Yinzhou | 342 | 368 | 392 | -7.1% | -12.8% | 92.4% |

Jan-Oct cumulative: Group sold 12,540 units vs. 14,320 units last year, -12.4% YoY, largely in line with Toyota’s regional decline (-2.83pp share loss). No store achieved its annual target pace (83.3% time progress vs. average 78.5% target completion).

Analysis by store:

* **Hangzhou Chengxi (largest, 428 units):** As a Hangzhou urban store, it was most affected by Tesla and Zeekr. Model Y’s October promotion (RMB 10,000 insurance subsidy + 5-year 0-interest) took away at least 40-50 Highlander/Venza intenders. However, its Camry sales remained solid (118 units, 27.6% of store sales) thanks to the increased RMB 30,000 terminal discount this month, which we will analyze later. Its inventory depth is highest at 2.1 months, creating capital pressure.

* **Ningbo Yinzhou (342 units, best target completion 92.4%):** Best performer. The store manager decisively bundled “Wildlander + Frontlander” as a RMB 130,000-150,000 SUV combo, capturing county-level first-car buyers in Cixi and Yuyao. Wildlander sold 96 units in a single store, accounting for 28% of its sales. Its sales consultants’ test-drive conversion rate reached 31%, 5pp higher than Group average, indicating effective product explanation around reliability and low maintenance.

* **Wenzhou Ouhai (285 units, -14.9% YoY worst):** Wenzhou private economy is sensitive to price, and BYD’s penetration there exceeds 22%. Our Frontlander, despite dropping to RMB 90,800 base price, still lost to BYD Yuan PLUS and Song Pro, which offer green plates (free license, no purchase tax). The store also suffered from staff turnover – 3 gold-medal sales consultants left for NEV brands in Q3, and new staff closing rate is only 12% vs. 19% Group average.

* **Shaoxing Keqiao (231 units):** Smallest base but most balanced energy mix – HEV models (Camry Hybrid, Highlander Hybrid, Sienna Hybrid) accounted for 58% of sales, highest in Group, reflecting Keqiao’s textile business owners’ preference for fuel economy and long-distance comfort. Sienna sold 28 units here, the highest single-store Sienna volume, proving MPV demand in family-business cities.

Gross profit per new car (including manufacturer rebates) fell to RMB 1,850 in October from RMB 4,320 in October last year. Highlander and Venza are now selling at a net loss after discount (see Section III), relying on finance commission and insurance rebates to break even.

#### 2.2 Used-Car Trade-in Volume: The Only Growth Engine

**Table 4: Used-Car Acquisition & Trade-in – October 2024**

| Store | Trade-in Units (Oct 24) | Oct 23 | YoY | Trade-in Penetration | Wholesale/Retail Ratio |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hangzhou Chengxi | 142 | 118 | +20.3% | 33.2% | 62:38 |

Jan-Oct cumulative trade-ins: 3,680 units, +18.2% YoY. This is a strategic success of our “trade-in for new + manufacturer replacement subsidy” policy launched in June.

Why did used cars grow against the trend? First, manufacturers offered RMB 5,000-10,000 replacement subsidies for Camry, Highlander and Sienna in October, which we stacked with local government trade-in subsidies (Zhejiang’s RMB 7,000 car renewal consumption voucher). Second, our used-car appraisal team adopted the “30-minute pricing + 7-day price guarantee” to improve conversion. Third, falling new-car prices actually stimulated used-car turnover – many customers who held 5-6 year old RAV4s and Corollas chose to trade in now before residual values fall further.

However, risks remain: used-car inventory days increased to 38 days (from 27 days last year), and average gross profit per used retail unit fell to RMB 2,100 (from RMB 3,800). Wenzhou’s wholesale ratio of 70% indicates weak local retail capacity for used cars. We are essentially using used cars to pull new cars, not making money from used cars themselves.

#### 2.3 After-Sales Service Data: Volume Stable, Value Up

After-sales is our profit ballast, contributing 71% of Group gross profit in October. Entries declined slightly due to fewer new-car owners and diversion to fast-repair chains (Tuhu, JD Auto) for out-of-warranty customers. But we successfully increased single-vehicle output through three measures: (1) promoting 40,000-km major maintenance packages for 2020-2021 Highlander/Camry owners; (2) tire + battery seasonal promotion (1,240 tires sold, +22% YoY); (3) boutique + extended warranty penetration reached 18.7%.

The warning signal is the 1st-year retention rate dropping to 68.5%. New NEV owners receive free maintenance and are less sensitive, but our new fuel/HEV owners are being lured by “free first 3 maintenances” from BYD and Geely. CSI also slipped 0.6 points, mainly complaints about “long waiting time for hybrid parts” and “service advisor over-selling.” Ningbo Yinzhou scored highest at 97.1, while Hangzhou Chengxi, with the largest volume, scored lowest at 95.4 and needs rectification.

### III. In-Depth Analysis of Key Models: Market Performance, Pricing Strategy and Promotion Effectiveness

Our six monitored key models cover three segments: Sedan (Camry), SUV (Highlander, Wildlander, Frontlander, Venza), MPV (Sienna). Together they accounted for 78.4% of Group October sales. All are currently at historic maximum discounts.

**Table 6: Key Models Price and Promotion Summary (as of late October 2024)**

| Model | Representative Trim | Guide Price | Terminal Discount | Base Price After Discount | On-Road Price | Group Oct Sales / YoY |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Highlander | 2024 2.5L Hybrid AWD Supreme 7-seat | 325,800 | 80,000 | 245,800 | ~272,000 | 168 / -18.4% |
| Wildlander | 2024 2.0L CVT 2WD Leading | 173,800 | 44,000 | 129,800 | ~145,000 | 312 / -5.5% |
| Frontlander | 2024 2.0L CVT Elite | 125,800 | 35,000 | 90,800 | ~103,000 | 268 / +8.5% |
| Camry | 2024 Hybrid 2.0HG VP Luxury | 189,800 | 30,000 | 159,800 | ~179,100 | 342 / -9.0% |
| Venza | 2024 2.5L Hybrid 2WD Premium | 265,800 | 65,000 | 200,800 | ~222,000 | 46 / -52.1% |
| Sienna | 2024 2.5L Hybrid Comfort | 299,800 | 25,000 | 274,800 | ~305,000 | 92 / -6.1% |

#### 3.1 Highlander: RMB 80,000 Discount – From Premium to Price-for-Volume, Effect Limited

The Highlander is the most emotional model. Everyone remembers 2021-2022 when the 4th-generation Highlander required a RMB 20,000-30,000 decoration premium and a 2-3 month wait. Now the 2024 2.5L Intelligent Hybrid AWD Supreme 7-seater with a guide price of RMB 325,800 offers a terminal discount of up to RMB 80,000, bringing the base price down to RMB 245,800 (on-road around RMB 272,000). This is a 24.5% discount rate, the highest among all Toyota SUVs in China.

Positioned as a mid-size SUV, nearly 5 meters long and 2 meters wide, with an imposing presence and 7-seat practicality plus Toyota hybrid fuel economy (6.5L/100km), the Highlander’s product power is still intact. Our October promotion – “RMB 80,000 direct drop + 0 down payment + 5-year low interest + RMB 8,000 replacement subsidy” – generated the highest showroom inquiries in the Group (1,850 batches, +25% MoM). But actual Group sales were only 168 units, down 18.4% YoY.

Why is elasticity so low? Three reasons: (1) Direct competition from BYD Tang DM-i Honor Edition (RMB 179,800起, green plate, 7-seat, intelligent cockpit) and Li Auto L7/L8 (extended-range, refrigerator-TV-sofa) has redefined “family flagship SUV” expectations. Customers who can afford RMB 250,000 now ask about lidar and urban NOA, which Highlander cannot provide. (2) The huge discount has destroyed price expectations and residual value confidence. Many intenders are waiting for RMB 90,000-100,000 off, adopting a wait-and-see attitude. Second-hand Highlander prices have collapsed 18% YoY, scaring off upgrade buyers. (3) Internal cannibalization: the new Prado (starting RMB 459,800) and Sienna divert some high-budget 7-seat demand.

Effectiveness assessment: Traffic effect ★★★★★, volume effect ★★☆☆☆, profit effect ★☆☆☆☆ (single-car loss ~RMB 8,000-12,000 before rebate). Recommendation: Maintain RMB 70,000-80,000 discount but stop further bleeding. Shift selling point from price to “hybrid long-distance reliability +保值 + 7-seat刚需”, bundle with 5-year free maintenance to lock in after-sales, and control inventory to 1.5 months to avoid踩踏.

#### 3.2 Wildlander & Frontlander: Compact SUV Duo – Most Effective Price-for-Volume

Wildlander currently offers up to RMB 44,000 off. Taking the 2024 2.0L CVT 2WD Leading Edition (guide RMB 173,800) as an example, the base price after discount is only RMB 129,800, with total on-road price around RMB 145,000 including purchase tax, insurance and registration. Positioned as a compact SUV with 2.0L+CVT powertrain, its advantages are reliability and low maintenance, disadvantage is insufficient power – but for family commuting in Zhejiang counties, this is precisely the right demand.

Frontlander offers up to RMB 35,000 off. The 2024 2.0L CVT Elite Edition (guide RMB 125,800) drops to RMB 90,800 base, on-road around RMB 103,000. This breaks the RMB 100,000 psychological barrier, making it the cheapest Toyota SUV in history.

These two are our only YoY-resilient models: Wildlander sold 312 units (-5.5% YoY, far better than Group -12.8%), Frontlander sold 268 units (+8.5% YoY, the only growing model). Promotion effectiveness is highest:

* Wildlander’s RMB 129,800 base price directly confronts Honda CR-V (RMB 135,800 after discount) and VW Tharu (RMB 132,000), while undercutting BYD Song PLUS DM-i top trims. Its closing rate is 24%, highest among SUVs. Customers cite “joint-venture + hybrid-like fuel consumption (7.1L) + low failure rate” as reasons. The “insufficient power” weakness is mitigated by our sales script: “city driving is enough, maintenance is half of turbo.”

* Frontlander’s RMB 90,800 strategy is a classic entry conquest: 62% of buyers are first-time buyers under 30, 45% are female, many coming from Geely, Changan and used cars. The RMB 103,000 on-road price is only RMB 5,000-8,000 more than BYD Yuan UP top trim, but offers Toyota badge and larger space. Ningbo’s “Frontlander for daughter, Wildlander for father” family combo promotion sold 38 double-car orders in October.

Profit is thin (Wildlander ~RMB 500 profit, Frontlander ~breakeven), but they bring finance penetration (68%) and after-sales retention (75% 1st-year). They must be defended as volume base in November-December. Suggest keeping discounts stable, adding “RMB 2,000 fuel card + dashcam” instead of further cash drop to avoid pulling down Wildlander’s price system.

#### 3.3 Camry: RMB 30,000 Discount Increase – Sedan Flagship Under Siege

Camry’s terminal discount increased this month to around RMB 30,000. Taking the 2024 Hybrid 2.0HG VP Luxury Edition (guide RMB 189,800) as example, base price after discount is RMB 159,800, on-road around RMB 179,100. This is the largest Camry discount in the past two years (was RMB 18,000-22,000 in H1).

Camry sold 342 units Group-wide in October, -9.0% YoY, accounting for 26.6% of sales, still our No.1 single model. The increased discount did work MoM: inquiries +18%, orders +11% vs. September. The 2.0H hybrid system (4.2L/100km, quietness) is widely recognized, and the 9th-generation exterior/interior upgrade has attracted younger buyers (average age dropped from 38 to 34).

But the sedan market is the most brutal battlefield. In Zhejiang, Camry’s October segment share (B-class sedan) fell to 11.2% from 16.8% last year. Competitors: BYD Seal 06 DM-i (RMB 99,800-139,800, 2,100km range, green plate) sold 18,500 units regionally, 5x Camry; Tesla Model 3 Highland (RMB 231,900, 5-year 0-interest) diverted young tech buyers; VW Passat/Magotan with RMB 45,000-50,000 discounts (base RMB 139,800) undercut Camry’s fuel version.

Our analysis: Camry’s RMB 30,000 discount is necessary but insufficient to regain share; it only prevents collapse. The hybrid version now accounts for 61% of Camry sales (vs. 42% last year), indicating customers vote with wallets for fuel economy to compete with PHEVs. Promotion effectiveness: volume ★★★☆☆, profit ★★☆☆☆ (hybrid still has ~RMB 3,000 profit thanks to manufacturer hybrid subsidy, fuel version loss).

Next step: Do not expand to RMB 35,000+ across the board. Instead, implement “trim-differentiated” strategy: keep RMB 30,000 for 2.0H hybrid main trims, increase fuel 2.0G trims to RMB 33,000 to clear inventory, and launch “Camry old-owner referral RMB 3,000 fuel card” to leverage 120,000 Camry owners in Zhejiang.

#### 3.4 Venza: RMB 65,000 Discount Yet Only ~1,100 Units Nationally – A Positioning Failure

Venza is the most worrying case. This model sold only around 1,100 units nationally in October, essentially marginalized. Yet it currently offers huge discounts: entry and lower trims around RMB 53,000 off, higher trims even larger. Taking the 2024 2.5L Intelligent Hybrid 2WD Premium Edition (guide RMB 265,800, discount RMB 65,000) as example, base price is RMB 200,800, on-road around RMB 222,000.

RMB 222,000 for a Toyota hybrid mid-size coupe SUV with leather, JBL, and 5.3L fuel consumption sounds cost-effective, but the market says no. Group sold only 46 Venzas in October, -52.1% YoY, with 78 days inventory, highest in Group.

Root cause is not price but positioning: Venza is sandwiched between Wildlander (RMB 130,000) and Highlander (RMB 245,800). For RMB 200,800, customers can add RMB 45,000 to get a 7-seat Highlander, or save RMB 70,000 to get a Wildlander Hybrid with similar fuel economy. Compared to competitors, it lacks the luxury aura of Crown Sport, the intelligence of Tesla Model Y (RMB 249,900, 0-interest), and the green plate of BYD Tang. Our sales consultants themselves struggle to explain “who is Venza for?” – neither sporty nor family, neither cheap nor premium.

The RMB 65,000 discount has extremely low effectiveness: it generated only 210 inquiries Group-wide, and 70% of those converted to Highlander or RAV4 after comparison. Worse, it drags down Highlander’s price anchor – customers think “if Venza can drop 65,000, Highlander should drop 90,000.” Profit is a net loss of RMB 15,000 per car.

Recommendation: Stop using Venza for volume. Reduce order intake, keep 1-2 display cars per store, maintain RMB 53,000 discount for entry trims to preserve price system, and reposition Venza as a “niche exquisite hybrid” for female high-income users (promote starry white + light luxury interior),

索尼WH-1000XM5深度体验｜400美元涨价，到底值不值？XM4老用户换机实测

哈喽大家好，我是你们的老朋友阿测。作为一个从XM2就入坑的索尼党，XM4我整整用了两年，通勤、剪视频、出差全靠它。当初听说XM5要改模具、涨价到400美元/国行2999元的时候，我心里其实是打鼓的：XM4已经是天花板了，还能升级啥？

但真香定律还是来了。预售第一时间在京东下单了铂金银，用了整整三周，每天8-10小时高强度使用，今天就跟大家聊聊，这代“不能折叠”的旗舰，到底是不是智商税。

📦 一、开箱与设计：不能折叠了，我却真香了

开箱还是索尼熟悉的环保纸盒，没有塑料味，好评。打开看到耳机包的第一反应：怎么变大了？没错，因为这一代最大的争议点——**不能折叠了，只能转平**。

刚开始我也吐槽，这便携性不是倒退吗？但戴上三天后，我服了。

新的头梁是一体式极简设计，特别细，塑料感很强但很结实。戴在头上像发箍一样，最大的好处是**不压头发了**！以前戴XM4出门，摘下来头顶必塌，这代基本没这烦恼。头梁内侧是大面积蛋白皮+顶部厚厚的记忆棉，完全没有压头感。

耳罩也变圆润了，一体感更强，8颗麦克风藏得很好，几乎看不出来。左侧还是两颗实体键：电源/蓝牙配对、降噪模式切换，右侧触控板滑动切歌、调音量依然灵敏。保留了3.5mm有线口和USB-C口。

那个像叉子一样的转轴现在微微外扩，夹紧力比XM4稍大，密封性更好，但完全不夹头。整机只有250g，比XM4还轻了5g，我连续戴4、5个小时追剧+剪片，不闷汗也不疼。

要吐槽一点：这个新版的磨砂亲肤材质，**是真的沾油**！用两天耳罩上就有指纹印了，建议大家包里常备一块超细纤维布，强迫症慎入。

🎵 二、音质实测：人声、 bass、低频、高频分开聊

先说结论：XM5是典型的索尼暖声，均衡、宽松，杂食到离谱。

**人声（中频）：** 我用蔡琴《渡口》、陈奕迅《富士山下》测试，人声位置适中，不贴脸也不远，齿音控制得很好。打开App里的DSEE Extreme，用QQ音乐听普通MP3，人声的细节和厚度明显回来一点，暖暖的很耐听。

**低频：** 看《银河护卫队》开头，星爵降落莫拉格星那段，低频的氛围感一下就铺开了，等到《Hooked on a Feeling》响起，鼓点和吉他节奏感极强，量大但不轰头。听EDM和Hip-Hop的时候，那个弹性真的爽，动作戏爆炸的冲击感也能感受到。

**高频/解析：** 这是进步最大的地方。听巴赫《帕萨卡利亚》、亨德尔《萨拉班德》这种小编制古典，小提琴和中提琴的音色能清晰分开，声场比XM4又宽了一圈。支持LDAC+A AC，可惜还是没有aptX HD，安卓党记得在App里开“音质优先”。

App里的均衡器很好用，自带明亮、人声、重低音几个预设，我个人喜欢在默认上稍微拉高一点高频，通透感更好。

🔇 三、降噪实测：地铁、飞机、办公室三场景

这次XM5堆到了**8颗麦克风+ V1处理器+AI自适应**，是XM4的两倍，官方说主打优化高频降噪。

**地铁场景（最惊艳）：** 我每天坐纽约...哦不，上海2号线实测，以前XM4能过滤轰隆声，但刹车那种尖锐的“吱——”还是会漏进来。XM5基本把那声尖叫抹掉了，车厢报站声变得很远，戴上+放音乐，基本就是自己的世界。

**飞机/出差场景：** 上周飞了一趟北京，引擎的持续轰鸣声过滤得非常干净。更舒服的是它的环境音模式，空姐说话、登机广播透进来特别自然，没有那种“电子味”，从降噪切到环境音几乎没有提示音，过渡丝滑到察觉不到。

**办公室场景：** 敲键盘声、空调声、旁边同事小声聊天，基本消失。但有个小bug要说：“Speak-to-Chat”一说话就暂停的功能太灵敏了，我调到最低灵敏度，打个大哈欠它都给我暂停了，最后只能关掉。还有按需注意模式，用手捂住右耳罩就能临时听外面，买咖啡的时候超方便。

另外它会学习你的常用地点+动作，比如我一走路就自动从全降噪切到半透风，这个在App里都能自定义。

📞 四、通话与多点连接：打工人狂喜

以前用XM4在地铁口打电话，对方总说“你那边风好大”。这代8麦+AI降噪，打电话提升巨大。我在马路边、办公室开腾讯会议实测，人声很清晰，风噪和背景人声被压得很低，商务通话完全可用。

多点连接依然是同时连2台设备，我是iPhone+ iPad + MacBook轮着用，手机听播客，iPad视频一响，耳机“叮”一下半秒就切过去了，几乎无感。在App里就能切换设备，不用去蓝牙设置里折腾。

注意一个坑：**多点连接和LDAC不能同时用**。开了多点就会掉到AAC，想要听Hi-Res就得在App里手动关掉多点，鱼和熊掌不可兼得。

🔋 五、续航与快充：三天不充电的怪物

官方标称30小时（降噪开），我实测只多不少。三天重度使用：手机听播客+平板刷B站+电视看电影，每天8-10小时，第三天晚上才提示低电量。

快充是真的救命：支持USB PD，**充3分钟听3小时**。有次出门发现没电，刷牙洗脸的功夫插上，通勤一小时的电就回来了。就是盒子里不送充电头，得自己买。

✅ 总结：到底谁该买？谁该继续XM4？

用了三周，我觉得XM5是对得起2999这个涨价的，它不是小改款，是设计+降噪+佩戴的全方位大改。

**1. 给每天通勤的地铁党/学生党：闭眼入XM5。**
你最需要的高频降噪、轻便不夹头、超长续航，它全给了。不能折叠换来的是更好的密封性和舒适度，包大一点就行。

**2. 给经常飞的商务党：强烈推荐XM5。**
飞机降噪更彻底，通话质量提升巨大，多点连接手机+电脑无缝切换，3分钟快充救急，这都是出差刚需。

**3. 给挑剔的发烧友/器材党：可以买，但别抱过高期望。**
它的音质在无线降噪耳机里是T0级别，听流行、OST、古典都杂食。但如果你追求极致解析和有线推力，它还是比不过同价位有线大耳。建议LDAC+ DSEE Extreme+手动EQ一起开，体验最佳。

如果你手里有XM4，而且超爱折叠设计、预算有限，现在官方1999的XM4依然很香，继续用完全没问题。但如果你跟我一样，追求最新降噪、更好佩戴和通话，XM5这400美元，花得值。

优点：无线降噪天花板级音质 / 降噪更强且环境音极自然 / 佩戴舒适到忘记存在
缺点：贵 / 不能折叠体积变大 / 外壳太容易沾油

**Luckin Coffee: From Nothing to Something, Creating China's Coffee Dream**

*As told by founder, Lu Zhengyao*

Hello, I am Lu Zhengyao.

If you have ever stood in one of our little blue-cup stores in the morning rush, watching the steam rise and smelling that first rich aroma, you have already met me in a way. Not me as a person, but me as a wish. Because Luckin Coffee was never just a business plan to me. It was a personal promise I made to myself, to my team, and to every ordinary Chinese coffee drinker: that we, in China, deserve a truly good cup of coffee — fresh, affordable, and made with absolute sincerity.

Today I want to tell you our story, from nothing to something.

### 1. It Started With a Question

For many years, I worked in travel and mobility. I built UCAR from a small car rental company with a handful of cars into one of China's leading mobility platforms. I spent my life on the road, in airports, in meetings, in traffic jams. And everywhere I went, I drank coffee.

But I always felt something was wrong.

In China, coffee seemed to have only two choices. On one side, there was instant coffee in the office drawer — bitter, flat, something to keep you awake but never something to enjoy. On the other side, there was the big international café on the corner, with its comfortable sofas and beautiful cups, but a latte that cost 35 or 40 yuan. For most young office workers, students, and parents I knew, that was a luxury, not a daily habit. A treat for the weekend, not energy for Monday morning.

I would sit in those cafés and watch the long lines, and I would ask myself: Why? Why does a country with 1.4 billion hardworking, creative people not have its own cup of coffee that is both world-class in quality and close to the people in price? Why must good coffee be a symbol of distance, instead of a part of our daily life?

In America, Italy, Australia, coffee is life. In China, tea is our root, and I respect that deeply. But I also believed a new generation was ready. They were curious, open, fast-paced. They needed good coffee to accompany their dreams. China didn't lack coffee drinkers. China lacked a coffee made for China.

That question stayed with me for a long time, until in 2017, in Fuzhou, I decided I could no longer just think about it. I had to do it.

### 2. A Small Team With a Big Dream

People often imagine Luckin started with a lot of money and a big office. The truth is, we started with nothing but people and belief.

I called together a small founding team — friends and colleagues I trusted from different industries: technology, marketing, finance, food and beverage. None of us claimed to be coffee masters at the beginning. What we shared was a stubborn belief: China can make good coffee that meets international standards, and we can deliver it in a convenient, fast, and warm way.

We rented a small space. We put a whiteboard on the wall and wrote three words: Quality, Convenience, Affordability. We told each other, if we ever have to compromise one of them, we would rather slow down than betray our customers.

From day one, we benchmarked ourselves against the very best in the world, including Starbucks. Not out of arrogance, but out of respect. We wanted to learn from them, and then walk our own path — a path that belonged to China. They taught the world what a coffeehouse could be. We wanted to answer what a Chinese coffee habit could be.

I still remember our first tasting sessions. We sat around a plain table with dozens of small cups in front of us, slurping, taking notes, arguing until late at night. My clothes smelled of coffee for weeks. My wife laughed and said I had become a coffee bean myself. She was right. I had fallen in love.

### 3. Our Relentless Obsession: Just For One Good Cup

If you ask me what Luckin is most proud of, I will not first say how many stores we opened. I will say: that cup in your hand.

Because behind that seemingly simple cup is a journey of thousands of miles and countless sleepless nights. I want to tell you honestly how obsessive we have been, because quality is not a slogan for us. It is our conscience.

**First, the beans.** We insisted from the beginning on using only 100% high-quality Arabica beans. Not blends with Robusta to save cost. Only Arabica, grown at high altitudes where the air is thin, the sunshine is long, and the beans mature slowly to accumulate flavor.

I personally went with our sourcing team to origin countries. We walked into farms in Ethiopia's Yirgacheffe, in the highlands of Colombia, in the vast estates of Brazil. We bent down to touch the red coffee cherries with farmers whose hands were rough from picking. We learned that a truly good bean must be hand-picked at perfect ripeness, one by one. A machine cannot feel that.

We cupped more than 200 different bean samples from around the world. We failed again and again. Sometimes too sour, sometimes too bitter, sometimes no aroma at all. Finally, we found our answer in a masterful blend of premium beans from those three renowned regions. When brewed, it gives that balanced taste we love: a nutty aroma, a hint of chocolate, a smooth citrus finish, with a rich crema that holds like silk.

In 2018, when our Italian-style blend won the Gold Medal at the IIAC International Coffee Tasting Competition in Milan, I almost cried. It was proof that Chinese-selected beans, roasted for Chinese taste, could stand on a world stage.

**Second, roasting.** Good beans can be ruined by bad roasting. So we refused to leave this to chance. We built our own roasting factory in Fujian, with world-class Probat roasters, and invited World Barista Championship champions to be our masters and guardians of flavor. We developed a unique roasting curve — slightly deeper than light Nordic style, slightly lighter than dark Italian style — to suit the Chinese palate that loves mellow richness but not burnt bitterness.

Every batch is cupped and scored. If it does not reach our standard, we discard it. My team once told me we had thrown away a whole batch worth a lot of money because the roast was five seconds too long. I told them: You did right. We can lose money, but we cannot lose trust.

**Third, water, milk, and machines.** A cup of latte is 90% water and milk. So we obsessed over those too. We use filtered water tested to the optimal mineral balance. We partnered with top dairy suppliers to provide fresh, sweet milk that pairs perfectly with espresso, creating that velvety mouthfeel. For our black coffee lovers, we ensure the extraction temperature is controlled to 90-92 degrees, pressure at 9 bars, extraction in 20-27 seconds — no more, no less.

We equipped every store with high-end fully automatic espresso machines from Switzerland, calibrated every morning. We trained every barista for weeks, not just to press a button, but to understand coffee: to smell, to taste, to adjust. I often tell our young baristas: You are not making a drink. You are delivering someone's first moment of peace in a busy day. Please make it with heart.

This is why I say our pursuit has no end. Even today, I still join our tasting panel every quarter. I still ask: Can it be fresher? Can it be sweeter? Can it be more stable from Beijing to Shenzhen, from a cold winter morning to a hot summer afternoon? A good cup is never finished. It is only the beginning of the next better cup.

### 4. Technology With a Human Warmth

Many people know Luckin for its speed — thousands of stores in just a few years. They think we only relied on capital. But what truly supported that speed was technology, and behind that technology was a very warm intention: to save you time.

I watched too many office workers wait 20 minutes in line for coffee and be late for work. I thought: Why can't good coffee fit into a fast life?

So we pioneered a new model in China: order ahead on the app, pick up in store in minutes, no long queues, no wasted time. Small, smart pick-up stores close to offices, universities, and communities. Through data and AI, we learned what you like, when you need it, how to prepare your drink before you arrive so it is still hot when you take it.

Digital management runs through our whole chain — from bean procurement, roasting, logistics, to brewing and sales. This is not cold. This is how we keep every cup consistent and every price honest. By improving efficiency, we can give you world-class quality at around 15-20 yuan with our coupons, not 40 yuan. High quality should not mean high price. That has always been my belief.

### 5. Our Chinese Coffee Dream Continues

From nothing to something, Luckin has grown from that small team in Fuzhou to thousands of stores across China, becoming a brand that even Starbucks respects as a competitor. But in my heart, we are still at the starting line.

My dream has never changed: to create China's own coffee dream. Not to copy the West, but to let coffee take root in Chinese soil. To let a delivery driver at midnight, a nurse after a night shift, a college student before an exam, a young mother with her child — to let all of them be able to afford and enjoy a truly good cup.

Every time I walk past a Luckin store and see a young girl holding our little blue cup, smiling as she takes her first sip, I feel all our persistence was worth it. That smile is our reward.

We started from scratch. We had doubts, we had difficulties, we made mistakes. But we never gave up on quality, because coffee does not lie. You can taste sincerity.

So here is my promise to you, as the founder: As long as Luckin exists, we will continue to chase that perfect cup — from a distant farm to your hands — with relentless care. We will keep visiting origins, keep improving our roast, keep training our baristas, keep listening to you.

If you have not yet tried Luckin, I warmly invite you: Come and have a cup with us tomorrow morning. Not because it is famous, but because it is made sincerely for you.

This is our story. This is China's coffee dream. And you are a part of it.

Thank you for drinking Luckin, and thank you for believing with us that China can have its own great coffee.

*— Lu Zhengyao*
